articles.title: Rosamund Pike On Starring in Spiky Stage Drama 'Inter Alia': "I Like to Do Things That Are Provocative"
articles.summary: The actress makes her Broadway debut in the role, which sees her as a powerful criminal court judge who is "shaken to her core."
articles.content:
Before each theatrical run of Inter Alia , Rosamund Pike spends time in court.

She sits in on criminal cases to get a better sense of how the British legal system works, with a particular eye to how female judges act. In one instance, Pike heard a judge reprimand counsel with a stern “I have ruled on that,” and asked playwright Suzie Miller to add that into the script to help give her own character more authenticity and authority.

In preparing to play Jessica Parks, a judge juggling criminal court cases as well as worrying about and taking care of her teenage son, Pike also met with the female judges, as well as with 18-year-old boys to learn how they speak to one another and how they view women. Together, all of these learnings have stayed under the surface for Pike, and helped her bring forward a layered, lived-in portrayal as she approaches the role for a third time and makes her Broadway debut.

“I wanted there to be humor. I met so many wise, witty, thoughtful, kind female judges. I really wanted to represent them. I wanted it to be as nuanced as we could make it. I wanted the teenage life to be recognizable and current,” Pike said. “And I also, I suppose, the other big thing is I wanted Jessica to fall on her sword. I wanted her to be so shaken to her core the moral compass she felt was absolute no longer is. “

Pike first took on the role during the play’s world premiere at London’s National Theatre in 2025. At the time, it had been close to 15 years since the Oscar-nominee had been on stage, after last appearing in Hedda Gabler . She wanted to return in a “modern play that really speaks to now” and finally found that in Miller’s Inter Alia , which shows a woman whose prowess at work adjudicating sexual assault cases and speaking up for women is called into question when her own son is accused of rape.

“I like to do things that are provocative. I like to do things where people feel glad that they went to the theater , that they got something out of it emotionally, and that they felt something. I go to the theater because I want to feel something, and I want to think differently about things, and then I thought, ‘Well, I think this play might do that,’” said Pike, who is also known for her on-screen roles in Gone Girl , Saltburn and Pride and Prejudice .

The play, which had a subsequent West End run before heading to Broadway, is meant to be a kind of sister play to Prima Facie , Miller’s one-woman show which starred Jodie Comer in the West End and on Broadway in 2023. That play followed Comer as a defense barrister who begins by defending men accused of sexual assault and then confronts how the legal system treats women once she is a victim of assault.

While Pike has two fellow actors on stage with her, playing her son and her husband, who is at times loving, and, at times, jealous of her rise at work, much of the show relies on Pike ping-ponging between the naturalistic settings of her home life and speaking to unseen fellow lawyers and others and monologuing to the audience about motherhood and the challenges of raising a son in modern society, as well as revisiting the memory of a former incident with her son as a young child.

“It's a very unusual play, and I think that's what Susie handled so deftly was the different sort of threads of a woman's life and the bits you have narrative control over, and the bits you don't have narrative control over,” Pike said.

And so while the play has a lot of physical demands, including Pike kicking off the show as the leader of a rock band, Pike notes that it’s been the mental workload that’s been particularly taxing, as her character switches between the naturalistic and imagined worlds.

The Broadway run began previews Nov. 11, ahead of a Dec. 1 opening. Pike took home a 2026 Olivier Award for her London performance. Combining her research with her experience doing the prior runs has allowed her to move past the technical aspects of the play, like lines and the blocking, into a more fully realized experience.

“Every step of the way, she has surprised me, made me laugh. She's incredibly naughty, but fun. She works as hard as anyone I've ever met, and she's sort of relentless in going ‘I want to make this show mean the most it can mean,’” said director Justin Martin, who has been with the play since the beginning.

Her role, and the play itself evolves, he added, in relation to current events.

Speaking ahead of her first preview, news was swirling about an alleged sexual assault in 2024 at a Cornell University fraternity house, which would be the kind of case to come before Pike’s character in the play, and in keeping with the subjects the play raises.

Pike noted that audiences can’t help but bring events like this into the theater with them, which influences their experience of the play. While the text of the play itself doesn’t change, the newspapers on the family’s kitchen table on set show current headlines, which also feeds into their performances and her portrayal as a judge.

“I think our play affects people very deeply because of all the themes it discusses about family, about motherhood, about raising boys, about responsibility of boys. We're not going to materially change the play in any way, but that's what great art can do,” Pike said. “The arts can shed a light or hold a mirror up to our world in a way that is sometimes more truthful and allows us to access those feelings, because sometimes the real event is too close or too confusing for us to actually access an emotional response.”

From her own time in British courts, Pike said she was struck by the way in which she saw a legal system set up to test and sometimes undermine the stories of women who come forward with a rape case, which ends up being another traumatic experience for victims. This play, from Miller, a former lawyer, may help point to the flaws in the system, she notes, in addition to its broader themes about how to bring up boys in modern society.

“I've sat in court and watched so many men be found not guilty of sexual assault,” Pike said. “I think Susie Miller always wants to raise a conversation within the law.”

The luxury jeweler opened doors to a new boutique located at South Coast Plaza in Costa Mesa, Calif. The outpost marks the fourth Boucheron boutique opened in the United States in a little more than two years, and it follows the first American address in New York and other launches in Las Vegas and Los Angeles. It's also the latest opening at South Coast Plaza in the luxury space following September's debut of the newly designed Tiffany & Co. store.

articles.title: Scott Caan Thought He Got a Prank Text. It Was Actually David Fincher Wanting Him in 'Cliff Booth'
articles.summary: The veteran actor reunites with Brad Pitt in the 'Once Upon a Time in Hollywood' follow-up that sees him taking on manic 1970s TV star Charlie Peters, who's in desperate need of Cliff Booth's help.
articles.content:
[This story contains spoilers for The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth .]

Getting battered with warnings about scammer calls and texts is nothing new in today's world. So when Scott Caan got a message, "Hey, David Fincher wants to meet you" for The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth , understandably he thought, "I'm being punked."

"I was going to write back like, 'Whoever this is, leave me alone.' I thought somebody was playing a joke on me. Yeah, sure, you're texting me to come be in a Fincher movie. Yeah, I believe that for sure," the 50-year-old actor quips when The Hollywood Reporter caught up with him over Zoom just hours before he headed out to the film's U.K. premiere earlier this month. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV 'The Body' Star Kristina Bogic Just Wanted to Take Care of Anya: "A Lot of Young Women Can Relate" Movies 'Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' to Dominate Thanksgiving Box Office as 'Focker In-Law,' 'Hexed' Join Fray

But it wasn't a joke. The filmmaker's producer partner, Ceán Chaffin, was reaching out about the role of Charlie Peters after Quentin Tarantino — who wrote the Once Upon a Time in Hollywood sequel — and star Brad Pitt suggested Caan for the character.

Given that Tarantino is one of Caan's "favorite writers of all time," and he'd get to reunite with his Ocean's Eleven co-star Pitt, it was an easy yes. But then came the challenging part of taking on a character that "can seem a little crass and insane" on paper, he says, and figuring out, "How do I justify all this?"

Once Pitt's fan-favorite stuntman Cliff Booth gets entangled with Charlie, a popular yet manic 1970s TV star, he realizes he's not being hired as his stunt double, but rather as a fixer to handle a dangerous hitman situation Charlie has found himself in. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"I figure out a way to ground all of it. So none of it seems like an idea or a cliché or a character. I don't want anything to be cartoony," Caan says of how he approached his reckless, unintentionally comedic character on screen. "I want it to be real. And then I got to find a part of myself that is that wild, wild, wild guy."

But as an actor playing an actor, TV superstar Charlie Peters specifically, Caan wasn't just taking a singular role. He also had to embody all of Charlie's characters within the film's fictional shows… talk about a meta experience.

"A lot of people maybe might want to goof on the acting part of it, but David and I talked about it. My goal as Charlie Peters is to win Emmys," he explains, wanting those characters to be as "thorough and lived out and grounded" as anyone else he's portrayed.

Sounds like quite the undertaking, but Caan confesses it's "an actor's fantasy." He adds, "It's a dream to be able to play three or four different characters inside of the movie you've been wanting to make your whole life."

For any actor, Tarantino and Fincher are as high a pedigree creative team as it gets, which only adds to the pressure as a performer.

"I've been doing this for long enough where a lot of the time I go in there, and I feel like I need to help the writing or I need to help, maybe it's a young director," says Caan, who's been a fixture of the industry since the '90s. "Not in an egotistical way, but in a collaborative way." So showing up to set and knowing you're fully taken care of was a "very rare" experience for him. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

It also allowed Caan to fully commit to those scenes that will likely have audiences talking for ages, such as Charlie, Cliff and talent agent Karen Crosby's (played by Elizabeth Debicki) first meeting when Cliff suggests Charlie kill a pig as a method acting exercise. Caan's character was understandably bewildered by the thought initially.

"That first scene where we're talking about the pig and he gives me that suggestion … it felt like we were doing a one-act play," the Entourage actor says with excitement in his voice. "As far as fun, and we did that scene a lot of times, I've never gone home and felt like, wow, that was… I never felt anything like that. We just did a one-act play 50 times today, and full 10-minute takes of that scene, and it's all over the place."

That was only the beginning of Cliff and Charlie's chaotic journey that would unfold across the next hour, but for one unfortunate piggy, it would soon be the end, as Charlie takes Cliff's acting advice quite literally. In a moment of symbolism, it's "really the beginning of my nervous breakdown," Caan says of his once-confident character now panicking, drenched in pig's blood towards the end.

"This scene, it has to work. If this scene doesn't work, then the Charlie journey is not complete," he explains. "So I remember being really, really, really sad all day long, just trying to stay in a really upset place, and Fincher was paying attention, and he just had me do it again and again and again until we were exhausted. It was a very memorable day of shooting." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

While Cliff goes on to do Charlie's dirty work for him in the final showdown with the hitmen, Caan's character is left "having to deal with all of my demons, digging deep and sorting out all my trauma" that's got him to this point, he says.

Similar to how Charlie's storyline ends with a moment of reflection, that's also how Caan walked away from the movie, having wrapped his first collaboration with Fincher and Tarantino. "I wish we could start over right now," he admits.

The film also serves as the first major project Caan worked on following the death of his father and Hollywood icon James Caan in 2022 . Known for his intense, charismatic performances, Scott's Cliff Booth performance undoubtedly felt like a nod to his legacy.

"I think about him every day anyway, let alone when I'm going into doing something that I think that he would've appreciated, something that he would've been great in," he says of his dad.

But Caan is also working to build a Hollywood legacy of his own, one that already includes dozens of roles from energetic getaway driver Turk Malloy in the Ocean's Eleven franchise (and yes, he's "100 percent" down to reprise his role in Ocean's 14 ) to Detective Danny Williams in the Hawaii Five-0 reboot. And now, Charlie Peters in Cliff Booth and agent Nick Schaeffer in NCIS: New York .

Even with a stacked resume, Caan feels he's still not in a place in his career where he can be too picky about the opportunities that come his way, especially in an industry with a limited — and shrinking — number of jobs. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"I think we all would like to think that we're at a point in our career where we can pick and choose, but the truth of the matter is, I feel like when I was younger, I felt that way," he admits. "And as I get older and have been in the business for a long time, you're just kind of lucky to be working."

So when you get a text that Fincher wants to cast you in a film written by Tarantino, naturally it's going to feel pretty surreal, even for a veteran like Caan. Because even after decades in the business, he tells THR , "I'm just constantly trying to figure out what I want to be when I grow up, and I'm still doing that, and that's the fun of our business."

He quips with a laugh, "I'm still only in my 20s. I got a ways to go, you know what I mean?"

articles.title: Sakamoto Days Ends With Shonen Jump's Best 2026 Finale
articles.summary: Out of all five major Shonen Jump manga series that ended in 2026, Sakamoto Days had the best ending. 2026 has been a very important year for the manga and anime industry, witnessing several revolutionary changes and making a significant impact on the entertainment industry as a whole. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Out of all five major Shonen Jump manga series that ended in 2026, Sakamoto Days had the best ending. 2026 has been a very important year for the manga and anime industry, witnessing several revolutionary changes and making a significant impact on the entertainment industry as a whole. In the manga world, Shueisha's Shonen Jump magazine continues to be a leading force, producing many great manga series, several of which have come to an end this year. This is precisely because of how the magazine is embracing a new style, which has also brought about numerous changes. Among the different ways the magazine has evolved, it has also seen five major Shonen Jump series come to an end.

It all started with Jujutsu Kaisen 's sequel, Modulo , coming to an early end in March, followed by Chainsaw Man 's sudden conclusion in the same month, which took fans by surprise. Next, Black Clover , a series that had been running for more than 11 years, came to an end in July, followed by Blue Box . Sakamoto Days was also expected to end this year, as it had been in its final phase since last July. On November 22, the series finally came to a halt. However, out of all five Shonen Jump series that ended this year , Sakamoto Days has proven to have the best ending.

What makes Sakamoto Days ' ending better than those of the other major Shonen Jump series that ended in 2026 isn't that it does something exceptional, but that it fits its original premise better than the others. In that regard, Modulo and Chainsaw Man don't even come close, as both series have controversial endings, especially the latter. Fans are still hoping for a Chainsaw Man sequel that will fill in the gaps left by the elements the series missed. Meanwhile, Black Clover has arguably the most clichéd shonen ending, which makes it a perfect conclusion in its own way, but it was also predictable, and something fans could be content with. As for Blue Box , it closed the chapter on Taiki and Chono's high school years.

Arguably, Blue Box had the potential to stand out the most among them, but its ending ultimately focuses on closing this chapter while hinting at something even bigger and better ahead. Sakamoto Days , meanwhile, manages to end with enigmatic battle action that most shonen series cannot match. Its titular character is an assassin who can adapt to any situation, using everyday objects around him as weapons, making his fights unpredictable and often hilarious. Sakamoto and Slur's final battle is a testament to this. However, what takes it a step further is how the fight aligns with Sakamoto's identity as a family man.

Sakamoto using everyday household items to highlight that he is a husband and father is one of the most unique actions any shonen series has featured in years . It perfectly matches the importance of family that the series has represented since its beginning. As for the actual conclusion, the series ends in the best comical way possible, with its characters fitting perfectly into the story's structure.

These final moments stay true to what the series has always been about, avoiding anything overly grand or confusing and actually bringing things to a close. That is what makes Sakamoto Days the major manga series of 2026 that sticks the landing better than the other four series that also ended this year. How do you feel about Sakamoto Days ending? Where does it rank among your favorites of the year? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: Alexandra Daddario Had To Wear Lots Of Corsets In Hershey, But It Was ‘Fantastic’
articles.summary: They helped make some very sweet looks.
articles.content:
We talk a lot about Alexandra Daddario ’s style and her knack for hopping on trends like the little black dress and corsets . She’s also been open about her costumes for movies. For example, she’s talked a lot about wearing that iconic red swimsuit for Baywatch . Now, in her newest film, Hershey , she had to wear lots of corsets. When I asked her about that and the stunning period dresses she wore in this film, she told me why they were “fantastic.”

I can totally see how the corsets helped Daddario. While painful at times, they alter how you carry yourself. So, I’d imagine that having different ones for different times in her character's life helped her figure out how to stand, move around and evolve Kitty’s physicality.

I love how much these looks helped her get into character. As someone who has been a fan of Alexandra Daddario’s fashion game for years, I was looking forward to speaking with her about her outfits in Hershey , because they stand out so much. They’re beautiful and fitting for the time, and I think it’s so cool that they really helped the actress find her character.
